newsitem.title: USA: Firefighters mop up as Alaska blazes flame out.
newsitem.headline: Firefighters mop up as Alaska blazes flame out.

text.p: Crews assigned to contain blazes that at one time threatened some remote villages were packing up Thursday as wildfires in Alaska came under control, officials said.
The 573,000-acre Inowak fire, which threatened Athabaskan Indians in three Kuskokwim River villages, was no longer considered a risk to settlements.

The 126 firefighters still deployed there were breaking down their camps and removing equipment, said the Alaska Interagency Coordination Centre, the federal and state office that monitors Alaska wildfires.

Elsewhere in interior Alaska, crews completed work to contain an escaped portion of the 386,000-acre Simels fire northwest of McGrath, the centre said. Two crews were taken off duty there Thursday and one was to be released Friday, the centre said.

In total, 82 fires were still active Thursday, the centre said, with firefighters deployed on six of the blazes. Most were contained or burning in remote areas designated for no fire suppression, the centre said.
Statewide, 679 wildfires have burned 1.85 million acres this summer, the centre said.
That is the largest total of acres burned since 1990, when more than 3.1 million acres were burned.
The Alaska Interagency Coordination Centre combines efforts by the U.S. Bureau of Land Management and the Alaska Division of Forestry.
